A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(99m) Tc-P agents are useful in imaging acute myocardial infarccts because they localize in necrotic and other damaged cells and because of their selective affinity for tissue calcium stores, particularly in the presence of a low blood flow.

(99m) Tc-P uptake in the acute myocardial infraction is limited to necrosis and severe calcium overload. (99m)TC-P uptake in necrotic myocardium is related to the presence of calcium hydroxyapatit, amorphous calcium phosphates and calcium complexed to myofibrils. (99mTc-P) uptake in necrotics myocardium is also related to the presence and concentration of calcium in necrotic cells.

the uptake of (99)Tc-P by the myocardium after infarction is a result of a complex interaction of many factors, including the following: (1) the presence of a necrotic zone; (2) the presence of calcium; (3) the presence of serum proteins and (99)T-c; and (4) the presence of blood flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
(99m) Tc-P uptake in infarct is a function of tissue calcium stores.
(99m) Tc-P uptake in infarct myocardium is a function of the degree of calcium overload in the infarcts, and the calcium content in the infarction is not a function of the severity of the ischemia.
(99m)TC-P uptake is a function of the amount of calcium present and the amount of blood flow to the tissue.
